subject: Business Models
title: Payment Processing Fees
description: A micro-lesson that makes Payment Processing Fees usable.

hook.text: Every time you swipe a credit card, three companies quietly take a cut: 2-3% of the total.

buildup.text: The bank that issued your card, the payment network, and the merchant's processor each take a slice.

discovery.text: Visa processes $12 trillion in transactions annually. At 0.13% per swipe, that's $15 billion in revenue.

twist.text: Visa owns no money and takes no credit risk. It just runs the network. Pure transaction fees.

climax.text: Payment processing fees are invisible to consumers but represent one of the richest business models.

punchline.text: You never see the fee. Visa collects it on every swipe.

quiz.question: What role does Visa play in payments?

details.summary: Payment processing fees are charged as a percentage plus a fixed amount on every electronic transaction. Stripe charges 2.9% plus 30 cents per transaction, Visa and Mastercard collect interchange fees from merchants, and PayPal takes a cut of every payment it facilitates.
details.whyItMatters: Payment processing is a trillion-dollar industry built on tiny per-transaction fees compounding across billions of daily transactions..
takeaways: Small percentage fees compound across billions of daily transactions
The payments ecosystem splits fees between networks, issuers, and processors
Payment processing is a high-volume, low-margin infrastructure business

faq.question: How are credit card transaction fees split among participants?
faq.answer: A typical 2.9% fee splits between the issuing bank (1.5-2%), the card network like Visa (0.1-0.15%), and the payment processor like Stripe (the remainder). The merchant pays the total fee while each participant in the chain captures their portion of every transaction.

faq.question: Why have payment processing fees remained relatively stable?
faq.answer: Card networks operate as effective duopolies with strong network effects. Merchants accept high fees because refusing cards means losing sales. Regulations like the Durbin Amendment cap debit card fees but credit card interchange remains largely unregulated in the US.
